memoryText: Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Chronicles 16:34 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse comes from the song David gave to Asaph and his brothers on the day the ark was brought to Jerusalem. You will read the whole song in a few days, in 1 Chronicles 16. It is a verse that bridges the Chronicler’s world and yours.

“Oh give thanks to the LORD.” This is a command in the form of an invitation. The word for thanks means to acknowledge, to confess, to give credit where it is due. Thanks is not just a feeling but a public statement. We say out loud who God is and what he has done.

“For he is good.” The reason for thanks is God’s character. He is good in himself. Not just good to us when things go well, but good in his nature. Jesus said, “No one is good except God alone” (Mark 10:18). All goodness comes from him.

“For his steadfast love endures forever.” The Hebrew word is hesed, covenant love, loyal love. It is the love that sticks. The word “endures” says that it does not run out. After the exile, the returned community needed this assurance. They had seen the covenant curses fall. And yet his love was still there.

The verse recurs again and again in the Bible: in Ezra 3:11, in Psalm 136, and in Jeremiah 33:11. When something appears so many times in Scripture, God is telling us to remember it. It was the song of the people at every major moment: bringing the ark, dedicating the temple, laying the foundation. It can be your song too, at every turning point in your life.
weekInReview: This week you began the book of Chronicles with the great genealogies. You moved from Adam through Noah, Abraham, Israel, and Judah, and saw the royal line of David continue past the exile to Zerubbabel. You met Jabez, whose painful name did not decide his future, and the eastern tribes who cried out in battle and were heard. You read about the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers who served in worship, and you saw the list end with those who returned to Jerusalem. Along the way, you prayed three psalms: Psalm 115, against idols and for God’s glory alone; Psalm 71, the prayer of the aged believer; and Psalm 144, a prayer for deliverance and for a blessed people.
reflectionQuestions: The Chronicler’s lists told the exiles that they belonged. Where do you find assurance that you belong to God’s people?
Jabez prayed boldly for blessing. What bold prayer, consistent with God’s will, might you offer this week?
Jesus appears in a genealogy that includes sinners and outsiders. How does that shape the way you see your own family story?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he is good and his steadfast love endures forever.
Thank him for your place in his story.
